issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" entry in the error message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple of error message types contains "transcriber_error" twice. Harmless at runtime due to membership semantics, but it is direct evidence the set was assembled by copy-paste rather than checked against the upstream ElevenLabs error-handling spec. Deduplicate and promote the catalog to a named module-level frozenset (e.g., ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES) with a comment linking the docs URL, so duplicates become impossible by construction.

issues.description: Per-error-type log context and category prefixes lost in the consolidation
issues.detail: The previous code emitted distinct logger.error lines ("ElevenLabs auth error: ...", "ElevenLabs quota exceeded: ...") and prefixed push_error with the category ("Auth error:", "Quota exceeded:"). The new collapsed branch drops the logger.error calls entirely and emits a generic "Error: {error_msg}" for all 14 categories. Operators lose both the explicit severity signal in logs and the typed discriminator in pushed frames. Restore a logger.error(f"ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}") and include message_type in the push_error string, ideally driven by a {message_type: (log_prefix, frame_prefix)} table.

issues.description: _receive_messages termination contract with the outer reconnect loop is implicit and undocumented
issues.detail: The old code wrapped the loop in try/except and logged "WebSocket connection closed: {e}" before returning. The new code removes that wrapper, but the postcondition ("on normal close, return; on error, raise so the outer websocket_service reconnect loop can act") is left implicit. The next maintainer who sees an unhandled exception will likely reintroduce the swallowing try/except and the bug will return. Either restore an outer try/except with the diagnostic log, or add a docstring stating precondition, postcondition, and termination, and confirm the supertype loop in websocket_service.py is prepared for the propagation.

issues.description: Inner bare `except Exception` inside per-message loop still swallows arbitrary failures
issues.detail: The remaining try/except inside the async-for catches json.JSONDecodeError (reasonable) and then bare Exception, logging and continuing. This is the same anti-pattern that produced the original bug, just at a smaller scale: it converts programmer errors and half-broken-connection failures inside _process_response into a log line and continues the loop. State which exception classes _process_response is permitted to raise under a well-formed message and let everything else propagate.

The split into _process_messages (per-message parse-and-dispatch) and _receive_messages (lifecycle wrapper) was the right decomposition: a stateless transform wrapped by an error boundary. The bug was the swallowing try/except wrapping the loop, not the existence of two methods. The fix should subtract the bug, not the structure — keep _process_messages as a filter and remove only the outer try/except that masked the disconnect, restoring a single "stream ended, will reconnect" log at the lifecycle boundary.

changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a final newline ("\ No newline at end of file"). POSIX text-file convention and most tooling expect a trailing newline; concatenating changelog fragments will run lines together. One-byte fix.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR correctly identifies a real bug — the inner try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing websocket disconnects and starving the outer reconnect loop — and that removing the swallowing wrapper is the right structural move. However, the implementation has three substantive defects: a literal duplicate \"transcriber_error\" entry in the inline error-type tuple (symptom of copy-paste enumeration rather than spec-driven construction); loss of per-error-type logger.error calls and category prefixes when the 14 error types were collapsed into one branch; and an undocumented termination contract between _receive_messages and the outer websocket_service reconnect loop. Secondary concerns include a remaining bare `except Exception` inside the per-message loop (same anti-pattern at smaller scale), loss of the _process_messages / _receive_messages decomposition that the bug did not require deleting, and a missing trailing newline in the changelog. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix the duplicate, promote the error-type list to a named module-level frozenset, restore per-type log context, document the termination contract, and add the changelog newline.
